assessment: The observations suggest two fitting problems worth separating: larger-size construction errors and differences between customer and reference-table geometry. Neither cause is established. Any trial must honor size and design, use existing stock and machines, pass the five-cycle wash test, stay within 350 currency units and three weeks, and verify cutting waste by area at no more than 8%. Success remains at least 38 of 40 first placements, all ordered designs, and median cooperative time at most 32 minutes, including trial and adjustment work.

openings.claim: A size-dependent error in the common cutting allowance may contribute to larger-cover rework; verified size-specific cards and staged cutting could prevent that error propagating through the batch.
openings.delta: Sew and measure initial covers before releasing the remaining cuts, allowing supported allowance corrections while stock is still uncut.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, measured cut-to-finished dimensional errors should recur with a consistent sign within a size before washing. Errors appearing mainly after washing or changing with cloth direction would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Start with one ordered cover per size; record card dimensions, actual cuts, finished dimensions, fitting error, design, direction and operator. Repeat a problematic size before revising its card. Measure retained offcuts in both axes through the stipulated wash cycles. Hold further cuts until the proposed correction fits the area-waste budget; record work minutes and subsequent rework.
assumptions: Staged cutting fits the delivery window.
An allowance correction can be accommodated by remaining stock without excess waste.
Initial differences require replication because size, design and operator may be confounded.

openings.claim: Corner-pocket geometry may explain some installation failures independently of nominal tabletop length and width; matching pockets to measured corner shape could improve first placement.
openings.delta: Treat corner shape as an order-specific fitting input alongside the selected table size.
openings.prediction: Among tables with matching measured length and width, installation difficulty should track corner shape; a corner-matched pocket should remove that difficulty without changing the ordered size or design.
openings.probe: Request actual dimensions and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where available. Compare square and rounded corner fits using retained-offcut pocket trials. Verify a supported construction on an ordered cover at its specified table, including removal and the same five-cycle wash test, before wider adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include useful geometry contrasts.
Corner changes retain the ordered visible design and fit existing stock layouts.
Measurement and sewing time remain compatible with the batch target.
